title: Aura error report
description: What Aura POSTs to `errorReportingEndpoint` while `errorReporting` is on: one batch of ECS-shaped entries, sent with `Content-Type: application/json` and — only when `errorReportingApiKey` is set — an `Authorization: Bearer …` header. Nothing else is sent: no `Accept`, no `X-Requested-With`, no CSRF token, and no wrapper field beside `errors`. The client is native `fetch`, so a same-origin request carries the session cookie and a cross-origin one does not. A batch holds between 1 and 100 entries — the flush sends the whole queue, not `batchSize` of it — and every non-2xx response is retried four times and then re-queued behind an exponential backoff, so an endpoint that rejects a malformed batch will receive it forever.

errors.description: The flushed queue, oldest first. Never empty — a flush with nothing queued does not happen — and never longer than the client's `maxQueueSize` of 100.

errorEntry.description: One reported error. `additionalProperties` is open on purpose: a future Aura release may add fields, and a receiver that rejects the batch over one of them would reject it forever.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the **first** occurrence. Once the error repeats, `lastTimestamp` marks the most recent one.

component.description: Where the error came from — a validator name (`HeaderValidator`, `BodyValidator`, …), a store (`ApiResourcesStore`, `CoreStore`), or a component (`DestroyModal`).

message.description: Text written for the end user. It is translated through `labels`, so it is **not** a stable identifier — group on `key` instead.

key.description: Stable identifier of the error. Validators put the offending field name here; otherwise the store generates `component.action.type`. This is the field to group and deduplicate on.

details.description: Raw developer-facing text — a Zod issue path, an axios message. May contain a URL with its query string.

metadata.description: Free-form context. A schema violation carries `receivedValue` (the rejected value **verbatim**, which for `HeaderValidator` / `BodyValidator` is the whole response section) and `receivedType`; a failed request carries `kind`, `status` and `code`. Unbounded on the client — a receiver must cap it itself.

count.description: Occurrences merged into this entry. **Absent while the error happened once**, so the count is `count ?? 1`.

lastTimestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent occurrence. Absent until the error repeats.

id.description: Caller-supplied identifier. Aura never fills this in; it can only come from the host application's own `addError` call.

stack.description: Stack trace. Aura never fills this in either.

errorLevel.description: Copy of `severity`, kept for ECS compatibility. Aura marks it `@deprecated` and always fills it in; a receiver should read `severity`.

errorType.description: Error category. `validation` is a schema violation in the config or in the API response, `api` a failed request, `client` a wiring mistake in the host application.
